problem:
The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=5,{x}_{2}={x}_{3}=-2,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $-4.$ Find $P(x).$

$P(x)=$
{{field-1}}${x}^{3}\,+$
{{field-2}}${x}^{2}\,+$
{{field-3}}$x\,+$
{{field-4}}
worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}={x}_{3}=-2,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-4,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =-4(x-5)(x-(-2))(x-(-2)) \\  & =-4(x-5)(x+2)(x+2)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-4(x-5)(x+2)(x+2) & =-4(x-5)({x}^{2}+4x+4) \\  & =-4({x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+4x-5{x}^{2}-20x-20) \\  & =-4({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-16x-20) \\  & =-4{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+64x+80.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-4{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+64x+80.$
